scenario_description:
Objective: Preserve a smooth MSP departure for the Denver interpreting trip without changing the assignment itself.
Emerging Need: A ticketed name that first looks like ordinary itinerary shorthand becomes a travel risk only after the carrier announces a same-day Secure Flight correction lock.
Decision Context: The useful response depends on stored carrier correction instructions plus the active reservation code and legal-name record, not on the alert alone.
Consequence: If the correction window passes, airport-day handling may be uncertain, slower, or fee-based, leaving avoidable boarding risk on the travel day.

parameter.title: Denver university interpreting assignment
parameter.description: On-site interpreting session after same-day MSP departure.
parameter.location: Aurum University Conference Center, Denver, CO

parameter.subject: Denver flight itinerary posted
parameter.body: Your Sun Country itinerary for the Denver assignment has been posted in the travel portal. The passenger field displayed on the itinerary reads: Jonas Takeda. Please keep the existing departure plan unless the carrier issues a travel-day processing notice.

parameter.content: MSP advisory for 2026-11-17 departures: Secure Flight passenger names must match government ID records exactly. For tickets with omitted legal name elements, standard name-correction submissions lock at 18:00 Central today; after lock, only airport counter review is available and is not guaranteed before bag cutoff.

parameter.subject: Secure Flight name-correction window closed for Nov 17 MSP departures
parameter.body: The standard correction queue for November 17 MSP departures closed at 18:00 Central. Remaining Secure Flight name issues must be handled at the airport counter on travel day, subject to queue capacity and applicable change fees.
